He's always wearing those heavy work boots, the tan ones that scuff up the linoleum. He came over once and tracked mud all the way from the front door to the kitchen sink. I had just mopped, too. I use that pine-scented cleaner, it comes in a big green jug. You only need a little capful, but it makes the whole house smell like a forest. I went camping in a forest once, up near the mountains. Put thoughts in my mind? No, nobody can do that. That's... that's like science fiction or something. Like those movies with the aliens that have the big giant heads and the silver suits. Hear my thoughts? No, that's impossible, isn't it? I mean, thoughts are inside your head. It's like... like when you put something in a drawer and lock it. He was a good dog, though. A golden retriever mix. He loved chasing those little green tennis balls.\n\nDoctor: How long have you believed that your family and friends are hiding your money?\n\nPatient: Well, it started right around the time my income dropped... so, about a year and two months ago, I'd say. I remember because I was trying to figure out how to pay my light bill. The electric company, they send those envelopes with the little plastic windows, you know? And the paper is always that weird recycled gray color. I used to save those envelopes to write grocery lists on the back of them. My mom taught me that. She was always saving things, like butter tubs and glass jars. We had a whole cabinet just full of old jelly jars. The strawberry jelly was my favorite, the kind with the seeds still in it. You spread it on toast and the butter melts all into it... I used to eat that every morning before I stopped working. But yeah, it's been about a year and two months since they started hiding my money.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had a period when you needed much less sleep than usual and still felt full of energy?\n\nPatient: Less sleep? No, I don't think so. I sleep pretty regular, mostly. I mean, unless it's too hot in the room. I can't sleep if it's hot. I used to have this little box fan, you know, the square ones? I kept it right by the bed, pointing right at my face. It had three speeds, but the button for the highest speed got stuck, so I had to use a butter knife to pry it back up if I wanted to turn it down. I don't know why I kept that knife in the bedroom. Oh, I used to eat peanut butter crackers in bed sometimes. Just the cheap kind in the orange wrapper. They always leave crumbs everywhere, though. You wake up and it feels like you're sleeping in sand. I went to the beach once when I was a kid and got sand all in my swimsuit, it was awful. It took days to wash it all out of my hair. But yeah, no, I just sleep normal, I guess. Nothing special about it.\n\nDoctor: Do you believe your family and friends are using special powers or technology to take or hide your money?\n\nPatient: Special powers? No, no, they don't have powers or... or technology. They're just regular people. My brother works at a hardware store, actually. He's always wearing those heavy work boots, the tan ones that scuff up the linoleum. He came over once and tracked mud all the way from the front door to the kitchen sink. I had just mopped, too. I use that pine-scented cleaner, it comes in a big green jug. You only need a little capful, but it makes the whole house smell like a forest. I went camping in a forest once, up near the mountains. We slept in this tent that smelled like old canvas and mildew. It rained the whole weekend, so we just sat inside playing card games. Go Fish, mostly. The cards got all damp and stuck together. I hate when things get sticky like that. Like when you spill syrup on the table and don't wipe it up fast enough. But no, they aren't using anything special like that, just... regular ways, I guess.\n\nDoctor: Have other people told you that your speech is hard to follow or jumps from topic to topic?\n\nPatient: Hard to follow? I... I don't think so. Nobody's ever said that to me. I mean, my mom used to tell me to slow down when I was little, but that was just because I'd get so excited about things. Like when the ice cream truck would come down our street. It played this song, I think it was \"Turkey in the Straw,\" but it sounded all tinny and warped, you know? Like a music box that was running out of steam. I always got the kind shaped like a baseball glove with a gumball right in the middle for a baseball. The gumball was always rock hard, though. You could break a tooth on it if you weren't careful. My cousin actually chipped his front tooth on a piece of hard candy once at a parade. We used to sit on the curb and wait for them to throw the candy, but you had to be fast because the bigger kids would just scoop it all up. He had to go to the dentist, the one over by the old strip mall that shut down. They put a big plywood board over the window where the shoe store used to be. But no, nobody says I'm hard to understand or anything. I just talk normal.\n\nDoctor: Have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy?\n\nPatient: Lost interest? I don't... no, I wouldn't say that. I still like the things I like. I watch my shows, you know. Mostly in the afternoons. The one with the judge, she has that wooden hammer... a gavel, right? She always bangs it so hard on the desk. I had a desk once, when I was in school, before I stopped going. It had all these carvings in the wood from the kids who sat there before me. Somebody carved a heart with an arrow through it, but the arrow was crooked. It looked more like a bent nail. My dad had a whole jar of rusty nails in the garage. He kept them in an old mayonnaise jar, the glass kind. You don't see glass jars for mayonnaise anymore, it's all plastic now. The plastic gets all greasy on the outside if you don't wipe it off. I hate when my hands get greasy. Like when you eat fried chicken at a picnic. We went to a picnic at the park by the lake, and the ducks kept trying to steal our bread. One of them actually bit my shoe. It didn't hurt, just felt weird. But no, I still enjoy things fine, I guess. Same as always.\n\nDoctor: Did this belief about your family and friends hiding your money come on all of a sudden?\n\nPatient: All of a sudden? I... I don't really know if it was sudden. I don't keep track of the days very good. My grandma used to have this big calendar on her fridge, right next to the ice maker. It had pictures of kittens in baskets for every month. The August one was a little orange kitten tangled up in green yarn. My cat got into my yarn once. I was trying to make a scarf, just a plain blue one, because it gets so cold in the winter. The draft comes right under the front door. We tried putting one of those heavy snake things, you know, the fabric tubes filled with beans or whatever, to stop the wind. But a mouse chewed a hole in it. Tiny little dry beans spilled everywhere on the rug. The vacuum couldn't even pick them all up. It's one of those old vacuums with the big cloth bag that puffs up like a balloon when you turn it on. It sounds like an airplane taking off, it's so loud. My ears ring if I use it too long. So... no, I don't know exactly when it started with the money. I just know they're doing it.\n\nDoctor: Do you believe your family and friends have done something impossible or supernatural to hide your money?\n\nPatient: Supernatural? I... no, I don't think it's magic or ghosts or anything like that. That's just silly. People don't do magic. They just... they hide things. Like how squirrels hide their acorns before the snow comes. I saw a squirrel bury a whole peanut in its shell right in the middle of Mrs. Gable's flower bed once. She had these big, bright yellow tulips. They only bloomed for a couple of weeks in the spring, and then the petals would just fall off, all over the sidewalk. They looked like little yellow boats when it rained and the water rushed down the gutter. I made a paper boat once out of a newspaper, the Sunday edition with the color comics. I liked the one with the big orange cat who loved lasagna. We had lasagna for dinner last week, but the edges got all burnt and crispy because the oven gets too hot on the left side. You have to turn the pan halfway through if you want it to bake even. The timer on the stove doesn't buzz anymore, it just makes this weak little clicking sound. So you really have to watch the clock on the wall. The clock with the big red second hand that sweeps around... but no, it's not impossible what they're doing with my money. They're just doing it.\n\nDoctor: Has your way of talking been like this for most of your life, or is it something that started around the time you began believing your money was being hidden?\n\nPatient: My way of talking? I don't... I mean, this is just how I talk. I've always talked like this, I think. My mom used to say I could talk the ears off a brass monkey. We had a little brass monkey statue on the bookshelf in the hallway. It was supposed to be one of those \"hear no evil, see no evil\" things, but it was just the one monkey covering his eyes. His little brass fingers were all tarnished and green from people touching him. I tried to polish him once with that silver cream in the pink plastic tub, but it smelled so bad, like rotten eggs and chemicals. It made my eyes water. I had to open the window in the hall, the one with the screen that had a hole in it where a grasshopper got stuck. It was a huge green grasshopper, with those long, spiky legs. They make that weird clicking noise when they fly, like a tiny little motor. My brother caught one in a jar and fed it blades of grass, but it died anyway. He buried it in the backyard under the old oak tree. That tree dropped so many leaves in the fall, we'd rake them into massive piles and jump in them. They smelled so dusty and earthy. But yeah, I don't know, my talking hasn't changed. Just always been me.\n\nDoctor: Do you ever feel that someone can put thoughts into your mind?\n\nPatient: Put thoughts in my mind? No, nobody can do that. That's... that's like science fiction or something. Like those movies with the aliens that have the big giant heads and the silver suits. We watched one of those on a Friday night once. My dad used to make popcorn in this big metal pot on the stove, not the microwave kind. You had to shake the pot back and forth, back and forth, so the kernels wouldn't burn on the bottom. It sounded like a maraca. Shake, shake, pop, pop. We'd pour real melted butter over it, and it would make the popcorn shrink a little bit and get all soggy, but it tasted so good. I got a kernel stuck in my teeth once, way in the back, and it hurt for three days. I tried using a toothpick, but it just pushed it in deeper. Toothpicks always splinter anyway if you bite on them too hard. My uncle used to chew on toothpicks all the time after dinner. He had this plaid shirt he wore every single Sunday, red and black squares. It was flannel, and it was so soft from being washed a million times. The elbows were practically worn through. So, no, nobody's putting thoughts in my head. My thoughts are just mine.\n\nDoctor: Did your belief that they were hiding your money begin within a period of less than two weeks?\n\nPatient: Less than two weeks? I... I don't really know how fast it started. Time is kind of funny like that. Sometimes a week feels like a whole year, you know? Like when it rains every single day. We had a week like that last April. Just gray and pouring, non-stop. The gutters overflowed and made this huge puddle at the bottom of the driveway. It looked like a little lake. A pair of ducks actually landed in it one morning! A boy and a girl duck. The boy duck had that shiny green head that looks like velvet when the sun hits it. They were just paddling around in the driveway puddle, dipping their heads underwater to look for bugs or whatever ducks eat. I tried to throw them some bread, but my neighbor Mrs. Higgins yelled at me. She said bread is bad for ducks, it makes their stomachs swell up. She's always yelling about something, Mrs. Higgins. She has this little white dog, a poodle mix I think, that barks at every single car that drives by. It's a high-pitched, yappy bark that goes right through your ears. She ties him to the front porch with a long blue leash, and he just runs back and forth, back and forth, tangling himself around the porch railing. He got so tangled once he was practically hanging there, and she had to come out with scissors to cut the leash. It was a brand new leash, too. But... yeah, I'm not sure how long it took for the money thing to start. It just sort of... happened.\n\nDoctor: Have you had less facial expression or less emotion in your voice than you used to?\n\nPatient: Less emotion? I don't think so. I mean, my face is just my face, right? I guess sometimes people say I look tired, but that's just because I don't sleep well when it's hot out. The air conditioner in my window is so loud. It rattles. It sounds like a box of rocks in a washing machine. I tried putting a folded-up piece of cardboard under the corner to make it stop, but it didn't really work. The cardboard was from a pizza box. Pepperoni and mushroom. The mushrooms get all wrinkly and black when they bake them, they don't even look like mushrooms anymore. My cousin grows mushrooms in her basement. It's so dark and damp down there, it smells like wet dirt. She has these big plastic bags filled with sawdust and spores, and they just sprout right out of the plastic. It's kind of creepy, honestly. Like little alien fingers pushing out. She gave me some to cook once, but I threw them away because I was scared they were poisonous. You hear stories about people eating the wrong mushroom and just dropping dead in the woods. So, yeah, no, my face is fine, my voice is fine.\n\nDoctor: Aside from the money, do you believe anyone is trying to harm you or plot against you?\n\nPatient: Harm me? No, nobody is trying to hurt me or anything like that. It's just the money they're after. People get so crazy about money, you know? Like my aunt, she used to buy those scratch-off lottery tickets every single Tuesday. She said Tuesday was her lucky day because she was born on a Tuesday. She'd buy five of the shiny gold ones, the ones that cost five dollars each, and sit at her kitchen table scratching them with a special silver coin. It was a quarter from 1976, the Bicentennial one with the drummer boy on the back. She said the regular eagle quarters didn't work. One time she actually won fifty bucks, and she went right out and bought a huge ham for Sunday dinner. It was one of those spiral-cut hams with the sweet glaze on the outside, and it came with a little packet of extra sugar to melt over it. We ate ham sandwiches for a week after that. White bread, yellow mustard, and a slice of American cheese. The cheese always sticks to the roof of your mouth if you don't drink enough water with it. I prefer Swiss cheese, honestly. The holes in it are so funny. I used to look through them like a telescope when I was a kid. So, no, nobody's plotting to hurt me, just the money thing.\n\nDoctor: Have there ever been times when, besides the money belief, you were very confused or your behavior got so disorganized that other people were worried about you?\n\nPatient: Confused? I like the green ones, Granny Smiths, they're so sour they make your jaw tingle. My grandma used to bake pies with them. She always burnt the edges just a tiny bit, but I liked it that way. The burnt crust tasted like caramel. She kept her flour in this big ceramic jar shaped like a fat chef. The chef had a little painted mustache that was chipping off. So no, nobody's ever been worried about me being disorganized or anything. I'm perfectly fine.\n\nDoctor: Do you ever feel that other people can hear your thoughts?\n\nPatient: Hear my thoughts? No, that's impossible, isn't it? I mean, thoughts are inside your head. I ordered pancakes, but they came out all burnt on the bottom. The waitress had bright blue eyeshadow, like, really bright, almost neon. She kept calling me \"hon,\" which I didn't mind, but she smelled strongly of peppermint. Like she'd eaten a whole bag of those little red and white striped candies. No, no, they don't have powers or... or technology. They're just regular people. My brother works at a hardware store, actually. He's always wearing those heavy work boots, the tan ones that scuff up the linoleum. He came over once and tracked mud all the way from the front door to the kitchen sink. I had just mopped, too. I use that pine-scented cleaner, it comes in a big green jug. You only need a little capful, but it makes the whole house smell like a forest. I went camping in a forest once, up near the mountains. We slept in this tent that smelled like old canvas and mildew. It rained the whole weekend, so we just sat inside playing card games. Go Fish, mostly. The cards got all damp and stuck together. I hate when things get sticky like that. Like when you spill syrup on the table and don't wipe it up fast enough. But no, they aren't using anything special like that, just... regular ways, I guess.\n\nDoctor: Have other people told you that your speech is hard to follow or jumps from topic to topic?\n\nPatient: Hard to follow? I... I don't think so. Nobody's ever said that to me. I mean, my mom used to tell me to slow down when I was little, but that was just because I'd get so excited about things. Like when the ice cream truck would come down our street. It played this song, I think it was \"Turkey in the Straw,\" but it sounded all tinny and warped, you know? Like a music box that was running out of steam. I always got the kind shaped like a baseball glove with a gumball right in the middle for a baseball. The gumball was always rock hard, though. You could break a tooth on it if you weren't careful. My cousin actually chipped his front tooth on a piece of hard candy once at a parade. We used to sit on the curb and wait for them to throw the candy, but you had to be fast because the bigger kids would just scoop it all up. He had to go to the dentist, the one over by the old strip mall that shut down. They put a big plywood board over the window where the shoe store used to be. But no, nobody says I'm hard to understand or anything. I just talk normal.\n\nDoctor: Have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy?\n\nPatient: Lost interest? I don't... no, I wouldn't say that. I still like the things I like. I watch my shows, you know. Mostly in the afternoons. The one with the judge, she has that wooden hammer... a gavel, right? She always bangs it so hard on the desk. I had a desk once, when I was in school, before I stopped going. It had all these carvings in the wood from the kids who sat there before me. Somebody carved a heart with an arrow through it, but the arrow was crooked. It looked more like a bent nail. My dad had a whole jar of rusty nails in the garage. He kept them in an old mayonnaise jar, the glass kind. You don't see glass jars for mayonnaise anymore, it's all plastic now. The plastic gets all greasy on the outside if you don't wipe it off. I hate when my hands get greasy. Like when you eat fried chicken at a picnic. We went to a picnic at the park by the lake, and the ducks kept trying to steal our bread. One of them actually bit my shoe. It didn't hurt, just felt weird. But no, I still enjoy things fine, I guess. Same as always.\n\nDoctor: Did this belief about your family and friends hiding your money come on all of a sudden?\n\nPatient: All of a sudden? I... I don't really know if it was sudden. I don't keep track of the days very good. My grandma used to have this big calendar on her fridge, right next to the ice maker. It had pictures of kittens in baskets for every month. The August one was a little orange kitten tangled up in green yarn. My cat got into my yarn once. I was trying to make a scarf, just a plain blue one, because it gets so cold in the winter. The draft comes right under the front door. We tried putting one of those heavy snake things, you know, the fabric tubes filled with beans or whatever, to stop the wind. But a mouse chewed a hole in it. Tiny little dry beans spilled everywhere on the rug. The vacuum couldn't even pick them all up. It's one of those old vacuums with the big cloth bag that puffs up like a balloon when you turn it on. It sounds like an airplane taking off, it's so loud. My ears ring if I use it too long. So... no, I don't know exactly when it started with the money. I just know they're doing it.\n\nDoctor: Do you believe your family and friends have done something impossible or supernatural to hide your money?\n\nPatient: Supernatural? I... no, I don't think it's magic or ghosts or anything like that. That's just silly. People don't do magic. They just... they hide things. Like how squirrels hide their acorns before the snow comes. I saw a squirrel bury a whole peanut in its shell right in the middle of Mrs. Gable's flower bed once. She had these big, bright yellow tulips. They only bloomed for a couple of weeks in the spring, and then the petals would just fall off, all over the sidewalk. They looked like little yellow boats when it rained and the water rushed down the gutter. I made a paper boat once out of a newspaper, the Sunday edition with the color comics. I liked the one with the big orange cat who loved lasagna. We had lasagna for dinner last week, but the edges got all burnt and crispy because the oven gets too hot on the left side. You have to turn the pan halfway through if you want it to bake even. The timer on the stove doesn't buzz anymore, it just makes this weak little clicking sound. So you really have to watch the clock on the wall. The clock with the big red second hand that sweeps around... but no, it's not impossible what they're doing with my money. They're just doing it.\n\nDoctor: Has your way of talking been like this for most of your life, or is it something that started around the time you began believing your money was being hidden?\n\nPatient: My way of talking? I don't... I mean, this is just how I talk. I've always talked like this, I think. My mom used to say I could talk the ears off a brass monkey. We had a little brass monkey statue on the bookshelf in the hallway. It was supposed to be one of those \"hear no evil, see no evil\" things, but it was just the one monkey covering his eyes. His little brass fingers were all tarnished and green from people touching him. I tried to polish him once with that silver cream in the pink plastic tub, but it smelled so bad, like rotten eggs and chemicals. It made my eyes water. I had to open the window in the hall, the one with the screen that had a hole in it where a grasshopper got stuck. It was a huge green grasshopper, with those long, spiky legs. They make that weird clicking noise when they fly, like a tiny little motor. My brother caught one in a jar and fed it blades of grass, but it died anyway. He buried it in the backyard under the old oak tree. That tree dropped so many leaves in the fall, we'd rake them into massive piles and jump in them. They smelled so dusty and earthy. But yeah, I don't know, my talking hasn't changed. Just always been me.\n\nDoctor: Do you ever feel that someone can put thoughts into your mind?\n\nPatient: Put thoughts in my mind? No, nobody can do that. That's... that's like science fiction or something. Like those movies with the aliens that have the big giant heads and the silver suits. We watched one of those on a Friday night once. My dad used to make popcorn in this big metal pot on the stove, not the microwave kind. You had to shake the pot back and forth, back and forth, so the kernels wouldn't burn on the bottom. It sounded like a maraca. Shake, shake, pop, pop. We'd pour real melted butter over it, and it would make the popcorn shrink a little bit and get all soggy, but it tasted so good. I got a kernel stuck in my teeth once, way in the back, and it hurt for three days. I tried using a toothpick, but it just pushed it in deeper. Toothpicks always splinter anyway if you bite on them too hard. My uncle used to chew on toothpicks all the time after dinner. He had this plaid shirt he wore every single Sunday, red and black squares. It was flannel, and it was so soft from being washed a million times. The elbows were practically worn through. So, no, nobody's putting thoughts in my head. My thoughts are just mine.\n\nDoctor: Did your belief that they were hiding your money begin within a period of less than two weeks?\n\nPatient: Less than two weeks? I... I don't really know how fast it started. Time is kind of funny like that. Sometimes a week feels like a whole year, you know? Like when it rains every single day. We had a week like that last April. Just gray and pouring, non-stop. The gutters overflowed and made this huge puddle at the bottom of the driveway. It looked like a little lake. A pair of ducks actually landed in it one morning! A boy and a girl duck. The boy duck had that shiny green head that looks like velvet when the sun hits it. They were just paddling around in the driveway puddle, dipping their heads underwater to look for bugs or whatever ducks eat. I tried to throw them some bread, but my neighbor Mrs. Higgins yelled at me. She said bread is bad for ducks, it makes their stomachs swell up. She's always yelling about something, Mrs. Higgins. She has this little white dog, a poodle mix I think, that barks at every single car that drives by. It's a high-pitched, yappy bark that goes right through your ears. She ties him to the front porch with a long blue leash, and he just runs back and forth, back and forth, tangling himself around the porch railing. He got so tangled once he was practically hanging there, and she had to come out with scissors to cut the leash. It was a brand new leash, too. But... yeah, I'm not sure how long it took for the money thing to start. It just sort of... happened.\n\nDoctor: Have you had less facial expression or less emotion in your voice than you used to?\n\nPatient: Less emotion? I don't think so. I mean, my face is just my face, right? I guess sometimes people say I look tired, but that's just because I don't sleep well when it's hot out. The air conditioner in my window is so loud. It rattles. It sounds like a box of rocks in a washing machine. I tried putting a folded-up piece of cardboard under the corner to make it stop, but it didn't really work. The cardboard was from a pizza box. Pepperoni and mushroom. The mushrooms get all wrinkly and black when they bake them, they don't even look like mushrooms anymore. My cousin grows mushrooms in her basement. It's so dark and damp down there, it smells like wet dirt. She has these big plastic bags filled with sawdust and spores, and they just sprout right out of the plastic. It's kind of creepy, honestly. Like little alien fingers pushing out. She gave me some to cook once, but I threw them away because I was scared they were poisonous. You hear stories about people eating the wrong mushroom and just dropping dead in the woods. So, yeah, no, my face is fine, my voice is fine.\n\nDoctor: Aside from the money, do you believe anyone is trying to harm you or plot against you?\n\nPatient: Harm me? No, nobody is trying to hurt me or anything like that. It's just the money they're after. People get so crazy about money, you know? Like my aunt, she used to buy those scratch-off lottery tickets every single Tuesday. She said Tuesday was her lucky day because she was born on a Tuesday. She'd buy five of the shiny gold ones, the ones that cost five dollars each, and sit at her kitchen table scratching them with a special silver coin. It was a quarter from 1976, the Bicentennial one with the drummer boy on the back. She said the regular eagle quarters didn't work. One time she actually won fifty bucks, and she went right out and bought a huge ham for Sunday dinner. It was one of those spiral-cut hams with the sweet glaze on the outside, and it came with a little packet of extra sugar to melt over it. We ate ham sandwiches for a week after that. White bread, yellow mustard, and a slice of American cheese. The cheese always sticks to the roof of your mouth if you don't drink enough water with it. I prefer Swiss cheese, honestly. The holes in it are so funny. I used to look through them like a telescope when I was a kid. So, no, nobody's plotting to hurt me, just the money thing.\n\nDoctor: Have there ever been times when, besides the money belief, you were very confused or your behavior got so disorganized that other people were worried about you?\n\nPatient: Confused? No, I don't think I've ever been confused like that. I mean, I keep my house clean, I do my own grocery shopping... well, usually on Thursdays. Thursday mornings are the best time to go because they restock the produce aisle. The apples are always so shiny on Thursdays. I like the green ones, Granny Smiths, they're so sour they make your jaw tingle. My grandma used to bake pies with them. She had this old rolling pin made of solid cherry wood, it was so heavy I could barely lift it when I was little. She'd roll the dough out so thin you could almost see through it, and then she'd cut it into strips to make a lattice pattern on top of the pie. She always burnt the edges just a tiny bit, but I liked it that way. The burnt crust tasted like caramel. She kept her flour in this big ceramic jar shaped like a fat chef. The chef had a little painted mustache that was chipping off. So no, nobody's ever been worried about me being disorganized or anything. I'm perfectly fine.\n\nDoctor: Do you ever feel that other people can hear your thoughts?\n\nPatient: Hear my thoughts? No, that's impossible, isn't it? I mean, thoughts are inside your head. It's like... like when you put something in a drawer and lock it. I have this little wooden box on my dresser, actually. It's got a tiny brass lock on it, the kind that looks like a heart. I lost the key years ago, though. It was on a red ribbon, a really thin velvet ribbon that I used to tie around my wrist. I think I left it at a diner once. It was this place off the highway that served breakfast all day, and they had these booths with red vinyl seats that squeaked every time you moved. I ordered pancakes, but they came out all burnt on the bottom. The waitress had bright blue eyeshadow, like, really bright, almost neon. She kept calling me \"hon,\" which I didn't mind, but she smelled strongly of peppermint. Like she'd eaten a whole bag of those little red and white striped candies. I tried making those candies once, but the sugar got too hot and ruined my favorite saucepan. It was a copper-bottom pan, really expensive. So, no, nobody can hear what I'm thinking.\n\nDoctor: When you say they are hiding your money, do you believe they physically took it or moved it in ordinary ways?\n\nPatient: Well, it's not like they just put it in a different account. I came in here because my family and friends, they keep saying the bank papers prove nothing was taken. But those papers are just... they're just paper. You can print anything on paper. Like those flyers they put under your windshield wipers at the grocery store. I always get them when I park near the cart return. Last week it was a flyer for a car wash, but the ink was all smudged because it had rained. It rained so hard on Tuesday, the gutters were overflowing and making this loud rushing sound. It sounded like a waterfall right outside my bedroom window. I used to love waterfalls when I was little. We went to this one park that had a huge waterfall, and the mist would get all over your face and make your hair frizzy. My mom used to carry this little pink comb in her purse to fix my hair, but it never worked. The comb had a tooth missing right in the middle. Anyway, for over a year I’ve known they’re hiding my money. They're using all these things to cover it up—like paying bills, or these fundraisers they talk about, or planning trips. It's all just a cover-up for where the money really went. So I just have to keep confronting them, you know? I have to keep asking them until they finally tell the truth. They think they can just distract me with all this talk about trips. I went on a trip to the beach once, and I found a perfect sand dollar, but it broke in my pocket on the way home. It just crumbled into dust."
